newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says China textile violations well documented.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says China textile violations well documented.

text.p: Chinese violations of a bilateral textile agreement were well documented and U.S. officials raised the issues a number of times with Beijing, the U.S. Trade Representative's office said on Monday.

China said on Sunday it planned to temporarily suspend imports of U.S. textiles, farm goods and alcoholic drinks in retaliation for U.S. enforcement actions against alleged violations of the textile accord. Beijing complained that the U.S. enacted its sanctions in a dispute over textile transshipments without full consultation or clear supporting evidence.

U.S. trade officials in September accused China of violating the accord by transshipping of millions of dollars of textiles to avoid U.S. quotas. USTR imposed punitive sanctions worth about $19 million against China. U.S. Trade Representative spokesman Jay Ziegler said on Monday that charges of transshipments were well documented.
"We have documented tens of millions of dollars in serious and repeated violations of our bilateral textiles agreement since 1994," Ziegler said.

"Each of the charges that we have enforced against China's textile and apparel quota has been carefully documented in U.S. Customs investigations. The number are not at all arbitrary," Ziegler said. U.S. officials have raised the issue a number of times with Chinese officials, he said.
The textile agreement is set to expire by the end of the year, and U.S. and Chinese trade officials are scheduled to begin a round of negotiations next week, Ziegler said.
China has often reacted to U.S. trade sanctions by countering with tit-for-tat retaliation.
